solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vessel behind heading for small Channel island

indicators.note: behind says the vessel word sits after the opening letter in the build
the heading of a word is its opening letter, so this takes the start of small

parts.note: Noah's ark is the classic vessel

explanation.surface: A boat trailing behind on its way to a tiny island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' tells you the vessel follows the S. Sark is one of the small Channel Islands between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small island in the Channel Islands group, near Guernsey, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Kind, like a senior nurse?

definitions.meaning: kind as an adjective, warm and caring as a sibling would be
in Britain a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward; the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.definitionFit: The word means affectionate and caring like a sibling, and also literally in the manner of a ward sister in a hospital.

clue.text: Quick attack trapping leader of pack

indicators.note: trapping means the attack word closes round another letter

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A swift assault that corners the head of a pack of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or swift, a straightforward synonym for quick.

clue.text: Pair watch, perhaps, for unfaithful partner

parts.note: a pair is two of something
a watch is one example of a timing device

explanation.surface: A couple's matching watches given as a gift to a cheating lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the watch as just one example of a timer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who two-times is cheating on a partner with another lover, so this is a synonym for a cheat in love.

clue.text: Daydreaming in court, appearing before large assembly

indicators.note: appearing before means the courting word comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a gathering is an assembly of people

explanation.surface: Someone drifting off in a courtroom while appearing in front of a big assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool-gathering is an idiom for idle daydreaming, from wandering about picking tufts of wool off hedges.

clue.text: Do exercises in school

definitions.meaning: to work out or practise physically, as an athlete does
school as a verb, to teach or instruct someone

explanation.definitionFit: An athlete trains by exercising, and to train a person is to school or instruct them.

clue.text: Rally rounding on head of state

indicators.note: rounding means the rally word goes around the word on

parts.note: a rally or protest march

explanation.surface: A demonstration that turns on the country's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a verb but is the noun, a protest MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, a king or queen, is the head of state in a kingdom, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Function of list, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word for list is taken by its sound

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone asking what a list is for, as they have heard it.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part or job something performs, a synonym for its function.

clue.text: Specimen supplied by son, more than enough

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A boy providing a generous specimen for testing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small portion taken for analysis, a synonym for a specimen.

clue.text: First half of song softly managed by old singer

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its opening two letters

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for softly
to run something is to manage it, so ran is its past tense

explanation.surface: Part of a song sung quietly by an elderly vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: SO is the first half of SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice range, so it is a kind of the definition.

clue.text: Invalidate yearbook, removing second article

indicators.note: removing means taking a piece out of the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
a is the indefinite article; here it is the second of the two As that goes

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike down a yearbook by cutting out its second feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second article' picks the second A of ANNUAL to remove, leaving ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, which is a synonym for making it invalid.

clue.text: Turn out to be point ahead

parts.note: the point of something is its end, as in the end of a stick
a team that is ahead is up, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A finding that something proves to be a point in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up as something is to finish or prove in the end to be it, an idiom matching the definition.

clue.text: Good access for aristocracy

parts.note: entry is a way in, or access

explanation.surface: Good access to the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed upper class just below the nobility, a close synonym for the aristocracy.

clue.text: Set off, went out in front, surprised

parts.note: to set off is to start out
a runner who went out in front led the race

explanation.surface: A racer who set out and took the lead, taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be given a sudden shock or fright, a synonym for surprised.

clue.text: Hate it, a late TV broadcast, but take no further action

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a late-night programme but decides not to complain about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the television scene but signals the rearrangement of HATE IT A LATE TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop at this point and not pursue the matter, which is to take no further action.

clue.text: Skilled worker from Hobart is a natural

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A craftsman from the Tasmanian city of Hobart is gifted by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across hobART IS A Natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson who works skilfully with their hands, a synonym for a skilled worker.

clue.text: Go home and go to bed

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in waiting your go in a game
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Head back to the house and then hit the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go home' reads as one instruction, but it splits into two pieces of wordplay; only the second half of the clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is an informal idiom for retiring for the night to sleep.

clue.text: Basic piano installed in flat

indicators.note: installed in means the piano is placed inside the word for flat

parts.note: flat beer or flat air is stale
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for softly, piano

explanation.surface: A basic piano fitted into an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home for the piano but means STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food or item is a basic, essential one, so the adjective is a synonym of basic.

clue.text: Herbivore filling saucepan, daily

indicators.note: filling means the letters sit inside the words saucepan and daily

explanation.surface: A plant-eating animal stuffed into the cooking pot every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across saucePAN DAily.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda eats almost nothing but bamboo, so it is an example of a plant-eater.

clue.text: Come back again about aggressive dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a cur is a snappy, ill-bred dog

explanation.surface: A vicious dog returns to the scene once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurs happens or appears again, a synonym of coming back once more.

clue.text: Company about to broadcast in capital

indicators.note: about means the company word goes around the broadcasting word

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A firm preparing to go on air in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Homeless child would appear in front, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A street child who would show up at the front of the queue first.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a neglected or abandoned child with no home, a synonym for a homeless child.

clue.text: Crime rendering rector powerless?

indicators.note: less means without, and P is the abbreviation for power, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest, a parson

explanation.surface: Something that leaves a vicar powerless, framed as a wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics abbreviation for power; removing it from PARSON leaves ARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property, so it is an example of a crime.

clue.text: First sign

definitions.meaning: coming at the start, as in the opening stage
to sign with the first letters of your names, as on a document

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means occurring at the beginning; as a verb it means to mark with your first letters, a form of signing.

clue.text: Dance enthusiast circling with energy

indicators.note: circling means the enthusiast word goes round the word for with

parts.note: a fan is a keen supporter or enthusiast
and joins things, as with does
go is energy or get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: A keen dancer twirling round with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' looks like a dance step in the surface, but it tells you the enthusiast goes round the word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance in triple time, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Supporting Democrat, unelected President

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: Backing a Democrat for a president nobody voted in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerald Ford became US President in 1974 without ever being elected either President or Vice-President.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford took office through Nixon's resignation and was never voted in nationally, which makes him the unelected head of state.
